title: Tumour Lysis Syndrome: Prevention, Recognition and Emergency Management

evidenceAudit.scope: Adults and children starting treatment for haematological cancers, and anyone with suspected tumour lysis syndrome (TLS) in the emergency department (ED), haematology or oncology ward: Cairo-Bishop laboratory and clinical definitions, risk grouping, hydration, allopurinol and rasburicase, monitoring and escalation to dialysis. Uses the NHS Lothian 2025 TLS guideline (based on British haematology guidance) and product information. Treatment of severe hyperkalaemia follows the hyperkalaemia topic.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 2026-10-22.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: No Saudi TLS guideline was found; the British Society for Haematology guideline itself was not opened.
NHS Lothian does not cover treatment of hyperkalaemia, hyperphosphataemia or hypocalcaemia, or criteria for critical care or renal referral beyond considering dialysis.
The fixed 3 mg prophylactic rasburicase dose is a local practice; the product information gives 0.20 mg/kg/day.
The allopurinol product information has no creatinine clearance table; the local rule (reduce to 100 mg if estimated glomerular filtration rate below 20 mL/min) is used.
Typical normal ranges for urate, phosphate, calcium and lactate dehydrogenase are not from these sources.
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.

pathophysiology.summary: TLS is a set of metabolic abnormalities after cancer treatment: laboratory TLS alone, or laboratory TLS with clinical problems (clinical TLS) (NHS Lothian TLS guideline 2025, Section Definition). It is defined from 3 days before to 7 days after treatment starts (NHS Lothian TLS guideline 2025, Section Definition). Risk rises with tumour burden: leukaemia with very high white cells, Burkitt and lymphoblastic lymphoma, and bulky lymphoma with high lactate dehydrogenase (NHS Lothian TLS guideline 2025, Section Risk). Rasburicase lowers uric acid but causes haemolysis in G6PD deficiency (Rasburicase SmPC, Sections 4.3 and 4.4).

symptoms: Reduced urine output (NHS Lothian TLS guideline 2025, Section Monitoring).
Palpitations or collapse from arrhythmia (NHS Lothian TLS guideline 2025, Section Definition).
Seizures (NHS Lothian TLS guideline 2025, Section Definition).
physicalSigns: Arrhythmia (NHS Lothian TLS guideline 2025, Section Definition).
Fluid overload or weight gain on twice-daily weighing (NHS Lothian TLS guideline 2025, Section Prevention).
Seizure activity (NHS Lothian TLS guideline 2025, Section Definition).
redFlags: Clinical TLS: creatinine 1.5 times the upper limit, arrhythmia, sudden death or seizure (NHS Lothian TLS guideline 2025, Section Definition).
Potassium 6.0 mmol/L or more (NHS Lothian TLS guideline 2025, Section Definition).
Rapid change in more than one marker (NHS Lothian TLS guideline 2025, Section Treatment).
No improvement with treatment: consider dialysis (NHS Lothian TLS guideline 2025, Section Treatment).
precipitants: Acute lymphoblastic or myeloid leukaemia with white cells 100 × 10⁹/L or more (NHS Lothian TLS guideline 2025, Section Risk).
Burkitt and lymphoblastic lymphoma (NHS Lothian TLS guideline 2025, Section Risk).
Stage III to IV non-Hodgkin lymphoma with lactate dehydrogenase twice the upper limit or bulky disease 8 cm or more (NHS Lothian TLS guideline 2025, Section Risk).
Chronic lymphocytic leukaemia during venetoclax dose increases (NHS Lothian TLS guideline 2025, Section Risk).
Past or current gout (NHS Lothian TLS guideline 2025, Section Risk).

differentials.condition: Acute kidney injury (AKI) from other causes
differentials.distinguishingFeatures: No rise in urate, potassium and phosphate after treatment starts (NHS Lothian TLS guideline 2025, Section Definition).

differentials.condition: Spurious low uric acid after rasburicase
differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Sample not chilled; rasburicase continues to act in the tube (Rasburicase SmPC, Section 4.4).

ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Defines laboratory TLS; after rasburicase use chilled heparin tubes on ice (NHS Lothian TLS guideline 2025, Section Definition; Rasburicase SmPC, Section 4.4).

clinicalManagement.title: Grade TLS risk before treatment
actions: Assign high, moderate or low risk (NHS Lothian TLS guideline 2025, Section Risk).
Screen G6PD in at-risk groups if rasburicase may be needed (NHS Lothian TLS guideline 2025, Section Rasburicase).

clinicalManagement.title: Prevent by risk group
clinicalManagement.timeframe: From up to 7 days before treatment
actions: Low risk: allopurinol (see Medicines) (NHS Lothian TLS guideline 2025, Section Prevention).
Moderate risk: allopurinol up to 7 days before treatment and at least 2 litres of oral fluid daily, or intravenous fluid if not drinking (NHS Lothian TLS guideline 2025, Section Prevention).
High risk: intravenous fluid with fluid balance chart and twice-daily weights, plus rasburicase up to 4 hours before treatment (NHS Lothian TLS guideline 2025, Section Prevention).

clinicalManagement.title: Monitor bloods
actions: High risk: urate, lactate dehydrogenase, urea, creatinine, electrolytes, calcium and phosphate up to 6-hourly until normal (NHS Lothian TLS guideline 2025, Section Monitoring).
Moderate risk: bloods before the first dose, 6 hours after, and before discharge (NHS Lothian TLS guideline 2025, Section Monitoring).
Send gel tubes on ice for analysis within 4 hours (NHS Lothian TLS guideline 2025, Section Monitoring).

clinicalManagement.title: Treat established TLS
actions: Give rasburicase 0.2 mg/kg for laboratory or clinical TLS, rapid change in more than one marker, or abnormal results after two prophylactic doses (NHS Lothian TLS guideline 2025, Section Treatment).
Treat hyperkalaemia by the hyperkalaemia pathway and discuss with the consultant (NHS Lothian TLS guideline 2025, Section Treatment).
Consider dialysis if results and clinical state do not improve (NHS Lothian TLS guideline 2025, Section Treatment).

regimens.indication: Prevention of hyperuricaemia in low or moderate TLS risk
regimens.patientGroup: Adults and children with low or moderate TLS risk
regimens.dose: Adults: 300 mg once daily; 100 mg once daily if estimated glomerular filtration rate below 20 mL/min (NHS Lothian TLS guideline 2025, Section Prevention). PAEDIATRIC under 15 years: 10 to 20 mg/kg/day, maximum 400 mg daily (Allopurinol SmPC, Section 4.2).
regimens.duration: From up to 7 days before treatment until TLS risk has passed
adjustments: Severe renal impairment: less than 100 mg daily may be needed (Allopurinol SmPC, Section 4.2).
Hepatic impairment: reduce the dose and check liver tests early (Allopurinol SmPC, Section 4.4).
With azathioprine or mercaptopurine: avoid; if unavoidable give one quarter of their usual dose (Allopurinol SmPC, Section 4.5).
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.
monitoring: Rash or severe skin reaction: stop at once (Allopurinol SmPC, Section 4.4).
Urate, creatinine and electrolytes as per risk group (NHS Lothian TLS guideline 2025, Section Monitoring).
contraindications: Consider HLA-B*5801 screening in high-prevalence groups before starting (Allopurinol SmPC, Section 4.4).

regimens.indication: Prevention of TLS in high risk
regimens.dose: 3 mg intravenously up to 4 hours before cancer treatment (NHS Lothian TLS guideline 2025, Section Prevention); product information dose 0.20 mg/kg once daily over 30 minutes in 50 mL 0.9% sodium chloride (Rasburicase SmPC, Section 4.2).
regimens.frequency: Once; repeat as directed by urate results
adjustments: No dose change in renal or hepatic impairment (Rasburicase SmPC, Section 4.2).
PAEDIATRIC: 0.20 mg/kg/day, no adjustment (Rasburicase SmPC, Section 4.2).
Screen G6PD in people of African, Mediterranean or Asian descent before use (NHS Lothian TLS guideline 2025, Section Rasburicase).
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.
monitoring: Uric acid in pre-chilled heparin tubes on ice, analysed within 4 hours, because rasburicase keeps working in the sample (Rasburicase SmPC, Section 4.4).
Watch for allergic reactions during infusion (Rasburicase SmPC, Section 4.4).
contraindications: Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency or other disorders causing haemolytic anaemia (Rasburicase SmPC, Section 4.3).
Stop permanently for severe allergy, haemolysis or methaemoglobinaemia (Rasburicase SmPC, Section 4.4).

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Two or more of: uric acid 0.476 mmol/L or more, potassium 6.0 mmol/L or more, phosphate 1.45 mmol/L or more, calcium 1.75 mmol/L or less, or a 25% change, from 3 days before to 7 days after treatment starts (NHS Lothian TLS guideline 2025, Section Definition).
Laboratory TLS plus creatinine 1.5 times upper limit or more, arrhythmia, sudden death or seizure (NHS Lothian TLS guideline 2025, Section Definition).
High, moderate or low by disease, white count, lactate dehydrogenase and bulk (NHS Lothian TLS guideline 2025, Section Risk).

teaching.scope: Adults and children starting treatment for haematological cancers, and anyone with suspected tumour lysis syndrome (TLS) in the emergency department (ED), haematology or oncology ward: Cairo-Bishop laboratory and clinical definitions, risk grouping, hydration, allopurinol and rasburicase, monitoring and escalation to dialysis. Uses the NHS Lothian 2025 TLS guideline (based on British haematology guidance) and product information. Treatment of severe hyperkalaemia follows the hyperkalaemia topic.
learningObjectives: Apply the laboratory and clinical TLS definitions.
Match allopurinol or rasburicase to risk.
Monitor bloods at the right frequency and escalate.
pitfalls: Unchilled uric acid samples giving false lows.
Starting allopurinol only on the day of chemotherapy.
keyPoints: Check G6PD before rasburicase in at-risk groups.
Chill uric acid samples after rasburicase.
Avoid allopurinol with azathioprine or mercaptopurine.

patientEducation: Your cancer treatment can release salts into the blood quickly; drinking well and blood tests keep you safe.
Report reduced urine, palpitations, cramps or fits at once.
lifestyleAndDiet: Drink at least 2 litres daily (not counting tea or coffee) if advised (NHS Lothian TLS guideline 2025, Section Prevention).
mdtReferrals: Haematologist or oncologist; acute oncology team; renal team for dialysis; pharmacist; nursing staff for fluid balance and weights.
dischargeCriteria: Bloods stable after treatment, urine output normal, no clinical TLS, follow-up blood tests arranged (NHS Lothian TLS guideline 2025, Section Monitoring).
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Repeat bloods before each further treatment cycle while TLS risk persists (NHS Lothian TLS guideline 2025, Section Monitoring).
